statement: For every real displacement delta in (-1/2, 1/2) and ordinate gamma in Real, the grade zero-character q = exp((delta + i*gamma)*log tau) is non-zero, and chi(K) = q^K is a character of the integer grade group (Z, +). The character group laws chi(K+J) = chi(K)chi(J), reflection defect B_rho(k) = 4 sinh^2(k delta log(tau)/2), and symmetric defect D_K(rho) = 4 sinh^2(K delta log(tau)/2) are smooth real-analytic functions of continuous delta, and conjugation/reflection symmetries admit arbitrary off-line displacements delta != 0. The symmetric quartet polynomial countermodel P_{delta,gamma}(z) = ((z-i*gamma)^2 - delta^2)((z+i*gamma)^2 - delta^2) satisfies all listed symmetries with delta != 0. Those listed symmetry and character premises alone therefore do not imply delta = 0 or force discrete quantization on delta.

quantified_variables.name: delta
quantified_variables.description: Real displacement from the critical line

object_studied: Grade zero-character chi(K) = q^K and symmetric defect D_K(rho)
fourier_normalization: Centered coordinates z = s - 1/2 = delta + it; tau = 2pi
order_of_limits: Evaluation for fixed K in Integer and continuous delta in (-1/2, 1/2)
exact_conclusion: Grade character and reflection symmetries hold for all real delta in (-1/2, 1/2); listed premises alone do not imply delta = 0 or quantize delta
logical_negation: The listed character laws and reflection symmetries mathematically force delta = 0 without additional arithmetic premises (FALSIFIED by smooth real-analytic family and polynomial countermodel P)
falsification_attempts: Evaluated D_K across delta in {0, 0.1, sqrt(2)/10, -sqrt(2)/10, log_tau(1.5)}
Verified that irrational delta = log_tau(1.5) yields rational modulus |q| = 1.5 in Q without arithmetic contradiction
Boundary dominance audit: as delta -> 0, D_K ~ (K*delta*log tau)^2; as delta -> 1/2, D_K remains finite and smooth
Verified exact root cancellation of quartet countermodel P at all 4 roots +/-delta +/- i*gamma to 80 dps

external_sources.source: Edwards, H.M. (1974), Riemann's Zeta Function, Academic Press

remaining_analytic_dependencies: Derivation of an arithmetic prime-zeta law that forces D_K(rho) = 0 (OPEN)
